applicability.fixture: Identical fixture: the same (id INT PRIMARY KEY, big BIT VARYING, small BIT VARYING) table, the same two rows with the same byte patterns and sizes, inserted in the same order, on a table the activation run owns exclusively in its own database. Revision 1 of the case (commit 37b1ceff8) differs from revision 2 (e64c16481) only in SQL keyword case and in the SELECT projections (revision 2 adds OCTET_LENGTH, BIT_LENGTH and MD5 columns); the CREATE TABLE and both INSERTs are the same statements, so the INSERT-side placement decision the evidence certifies is the same. The evidence referenced is revision 2's validated checker output; revision 1's own passive collector (activation_evidence.sh, docs commit a953d6f) ran on both installs but its outputs were not preserved, which is why this record points at the checker's.
applicability.execution_path: DIFFERENT run mode, which is why this is reused and not proven. The CTP invocation ran client-server over JDBC; the activation checker ran standalone under csql -S. The heap write path under test is server-side and identical in both, but the client transport and session layer are not. Certifies the INSERT-side demotion decision only; certifies no scan, recovery or vacuum path. ACCEPTED INTERPRETATION (user decision 2026-09-11, recorded in ticket 35, O2): the specification's 'execution path must match' is read as 'same OOS operation (insert, scan, recovery, vacuum), not same run mode'. Under that reading this evidence is applicable to the case; the run-mode mismatch is recorded here rather than quietly upgraded, and `reused` remains the correct status for ticket 13's rows. The map stays closed: this is the accepted interpretation of an existing rule, not a new design choice. Tickets 18 to 22 run their activation checks client-server under campaign_ns.sh in the case's own run mode, so the question stops arising for public SQL.
applicability.engine_configuration: Same pinned engine commit f4299ac0cd777a2a964c1f197ae5ebf9841a4936, same release install, same 16 KiB page size, unmodified build, no instrumentation. All nine assertions also pass identically on the pinned debug install (activation_debug.txt), so the observation is not release-specific.
applicability.conditions: Single session, no concurrency, no fault injection, empty table at the start, no vacuum or restart in between. SHOW HEAP OOS reports per class, so exclusive ownership of the table is what makes the chunk count attributable to this fixture.

outstanding_coverage.note: RECORDED AFTER THE FACT. This manifest describes ticket 13's revision-1 CTP invocation (case commit 37b1ceff8, green: Total:1 Success:1 Fail:0, execute_case:1, 39 s wall clock from 20:23:30 to 20:24:09, result directory schedule_linux_sql_64bit_1020240166, summary.info totalTime 67 ms). It was written on 2026-09-11 by ticket 35 from the retained bundle att-T13-0001, whose SHA256SUMS verifies, after the independent review of ticket 13 found (F6) that a complete, green, promoted attempt had a replay bundle and no record. Revision 1's oracle (expected-oracle.md, first part) fixed the assertion count at 15: 5 scalars per row group x 2, 3 in the final aggregate, and the two INSERT affected-row counts. executed.assertion_count IS NULL because CTP reports only Total, Success, Fail and execute_case and has no assertion counter; the 15 is derived from the case text and is justified only because CTP compares the whole result text (a byte-identical .result entails that all 15 matched). proof.verdict is 'proven' on what was observed: expected case count 1 == discovered 1 == executed 1, execute_case:1 in main.info, launcher exit 0, and a byte-identical comparison against the reviewed answer (candidate.result and expected.answer both sha256 bd64083a...). SUPERSESSION: revision 1's answer was replaced the same day by revision 2's (commit e64c16481, manifest inv-T13-0002) after the two-axis review; that is a revision of the case, not a FAIL of this attempt, so the attempt stays PASS and no matrix row records a FAIL for it. hasAnswer in this run's summary.info reads false although the answer existed and matched (ticket 13 report, finding d). CONFIGURATIONS_NOT_RUN RULE (ticket 35, F4): the list enumerates every page-size x build-mode x run-mode combination of the configuration domain (4096/8192/16384 x release/debug x standalone/client-server, 12 in all) that THE CTP CASE DID NOT RUN IN THIS INVOCATION; the invocation ran exactly one, 16384/release/client-server, so 11 are listed. The two standalone activation-checker runs (release and debug, 16 KiB) are evidence runs of the checker, not executions of the case, and are treated alike: neither removes an entry. Ticket 15's wrapper generates this field from the same rule. The 43 assertable requirements without an executed case are the same Delivery gap inv-T13-0002 lists.
